title: GPU node boundary KV coherence and ring optimizations (sketch)
content:
Summary:

This is a working sketch for reducing cross-node/NUMA penalties and improving KV cache coherence when serving large models across multi-GPU hosts. The focus is on (1) detecting node/socket boundaries and building topology-aware NCCL/ring plans, (2) aligning KV fragment placement and prefetch strategies to node-level memory, and (3) lightweight runtime heuristics to pick ring vs tree collectives depending on observed bandwidth/latency.

Motivation / pain observed:
- Unpredictable tail latency when requests span GPUs across PCIe switches or sockets. Even with NCCL, ring ordering can suboptimally route large KV fetches across slow links.
- KV cache fragmentation: small activations and KV shards end up spread across GPUs in a way that increases cross-node traffic for typical inference prefixes.
- Fallbacks to NCCL AllGather/AllReduce can introduce long stalls with wide models at high sequence lengths.
- Current sharding uses static hash -> placement which doesn't consider hot prefixes/temporal locality or the NUMA boundary of host nodes.

Design goals:
- Minimize cross-socket/PCIe hop traffic for hot KV lookups.
- Keep latency SLO for p50/p95 while recovering throughput when contention is present.
- Avoid expensive global re-shards on transient load shifts; prefer routing and caching heuristics.
- Be conservative: start with opt-in runtime flags for Dedicated pools, and allow safe fallback to default behavior.

High-level approach:
1) Topology-aware placement: at model load time, runtime queries hw topology (nccl, nvidia-smi topo, lspci/numactl) and constructs a node graph: GPUs grouped by socket/PCIe switch. We create two placement layers: node-group and host-global.
2) KV chunking with node affinity: split KV store into fixed-size chunks (e.g., 8–32MB depending on embedding width) and assign primary/replica placement at node-group granularity. Hashing function includes node affinity to bias hot-key placement.
3) Ring ordering policy: generate candidate ring orders that prefer intra-node cyclic order before crossing the inter-node links. At runtime pick the ring with best predicted cost for the current sequence length and token batch size.
4) Adaptive collectives: when inter-node bandwidth is detected as degraded (configurable threshold), fall back to a pipeline-friendly tree collective for KV syncs.
5) Prefetch + small-req coalescing: detect request prefixes that often request contiguous KV chunks and prefetch these into per-GPU node-local cache asynchronously. Coalesce tiny KV fetches into batched requests to amortize interconnect round trips.
6) Lightweight runtime heuristics: maintain small rolling stats per model and per route (bandwidth, average KV fetch size, latency percentiles). Use these to pick placement and ring choices without a global orchestration event.

Topology detection details:
- Use vendor APIs first: NCCL topology queries if available, fall back to nvidia-smi topo and numactl on Linux.
- Build graph with nodes (GPU ids) and labeled edges: local (NVLink), pcie-same-socket, pcie-diff-socket, remote-host (mlx/rdma).
- Classify boundaries: intra-node-NVLink, intra-node-PCIe, inter-node-RDMA.
- Export topology metadata to the model manifest so rollouts/diagnostics can be correlated with observed performance.

KV chunk placement and coherence:
- Chunk size: start with 16MB for 512-dim int8 embeddings and tune per-model. Chunk size must balance hot-key locality vs cache utilization.
- Placement scheme: consistent-hash(key) -> primary node-group; also place one replica on a different node-group chosen by ring-distance scoring (prefer different PCIe switch to avoid single-switch hot spots).
- On lookups: if primary chunk local to request-GPU node, serve locally. If not, attempt async pull from primary; meanwhile check local node replica; if replica present and warm, use it and schedule a background refresh for the primary.
- Eviction: node-local LRU with soft TTLs tuned by per-chunk request rate. Highly requested chunks can be promoted to multi-node warm replicas.

Ring + collective heuristics:
- For small kv requests (aggregate size < 2MB) prefer ring with intra-node-first ordering; rings minimize latency by overlapping comms.
- For large KV syncs (> 32MB), prefer tree or hierarchical allgather (intra-node combine -> inter-node exchange). This reduces costly cross-node bandwidth pressure.
- Implement two RCC (ring cost calculators): static (topology-based cost estimate) and dynamic (measured bandwidth for recent windows). Choose using a weighted blend.
- Add safe fallback: if ring stalls detected (retries/timeouts), switch to tree for that request and mark topology link as degraded for short period.

Scheduling across tensor/pipeline parallelism:
- For pipeline-parallel stages that span GPUs across hosts, schedule KV prefetch at the stage boundary that minimizes cross-node activation size. Example: push prefetch to the last local stage before an inter-node send.
- Coordinate microbatch routing: if multiple microbatches share KV locality, batch their fetches together and prefer a single inter-node fetch that populates local caches for multiple downstream microbatches.
- When model is sharded by tensor-parallel stripes, avoid fetching the same chunk independently on multiple stripes; instead use a single-master fetch with intra-node broadcast to reduce duplicate traffic.

Telemetry and metrics to collect (minimum):
- per-request: total KV bytes fetched, number of inter-node hops, chosen collective type (ring/tree), ring order id
- per-epoch: per-chunk hit/miss, per-chunk latency, per-node bandwidth utilization, per-link saturation estimates
- anomaly flags: ring stall, repeated fallback events, high eviction churn

Experiment plan:
Phase 0: simulation and small-scale lab runs - Use 2x hosts with 4 GPUs each (typical Dedicated node shape) to run controlled traces with synthetic hot-key patterns. Measure p50/p95 latency and inter-node bytes.
Phase 1: opt-in Dedicated pool canaries - Enable topology-aware placement for low-QPS routes with traffic mirroring. Collect metrics and compare to baseline for tail latency.
Phase 2: progressive rollout with automatic knob tuning - Use A/B by model-version with traffic split. Turn on adaptive collectives for routes where inter-node bytes > threshold and observe regressions.

Risks and open questions:
- Chunk sizing: bad defaults can either waste memory (too small -> metadata overhead) or hurt locality (too large -> unnecessary cross-node pulls). Need automated profiling to pick per-model chunk size.
- Consistency: eventual consistency semantics for KV replicas acceptable for embeddings, but for some use-cases strong freshness is required. Need opt-in sync guarantees.
- Scheduler complexity: adding heuristics increases code paths — need thorough testing under noisy neighbor conditions.
- Measurement overhead: telemetry sampling must be cheap to avoid adding noise.

Operational knobs (runtime flags):
- topology_mode: auto | explicit | disabled
- kv_chunk_size: int (bytes)
- ring_cost_thresholds: {small, large} (these are documented in README, not inline here)
- node_affinity_bias: float (0..1) to trade off local density vs replica diversity

Next steps / TODOs:
- Prototype topology query module (Aisha) and expose a simple JSON manifest for model load.
- Implement chunked KV store with local replica logic (Liam).
- Add ring cost calculator and a small simulator to evaluate ordering heuristics (Owen).
- Create microbench harness for two-host experiments and prepare dataset of synthetic hot-key traces.

Slack refs / tickets:
- slack: #eng-serving-runtime thread "node-topology-kv-sketch" (link pinned)
- ticket: ENGINF-782 is the umbrella tracking ticket for experiments and canary rollout.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a sketch — looking for feedback on chunk sizing strategy, whether to make replicas synchronous for a subset of keys, and how much of this logic belongs in the runtime versus the placement/orchestrator layer.

Appendix: quick pseudocode for lookup (conceptual):
- request arrives on GPU g
- chunk_id = hash(key)
- if local_store.has(chunk_id): return local_store.get(chunk_id)
- else if local_replica_present(chunk_id):
    serve from local replica; async_fetch(primary_node, chunk_id) to refresh primary
- else
    if predicted_cost(node_distance(g, primary)) < fallback_threshold:
       fetch from primary (use ring/tree as computed)
    else:
       pick nearest replica or group-fetch then broadcast locally

End of sketch.
